report:
Reviewed the fresh full crates.sage_ir.types.body.for_iteration claim and all associated implementation/test evidence. The claim requires a for expression to become an IntoIterator call followed by a structured loop and match. Conversion, ordering, loop structure and match structure are all necessary; retaining a source-shaped For node or checking its children is insufficient.

The only implementation association is the explicit sage_meta::todo marker in crates/sage-meta/tests/representation_spec.rs stating that for-loop iterator elaboration remains pending. The only associated test is sage_meta::todo::types_body_for_iteration. Its body is solely that TODO, with no assertions or behavioral execution. There are no ordinary or N/A entries. The placeholder therefore preserves an implementation and test gap, not a completed guarantee.

Captured the current For checker branch as a dependency. It checks the iterable expression, pushes a lexical scope, checks the pattern and body, pops the scope, and returns TyExprData::For with unit type. The inspected branch does not synthesize an IntoIterator call or transform the operation into loop/match nodes. This is concrete support for the existing elaboration prerequisite, not a newly discovered contradiction to a completeness claim. No behavior outside this branch is inferred as verified.

Captured the typed-IR destination table and accepted completed-tree architectural rationale. They place for-loop elaboration within structured typed trees; they do not require MIR basic blocks or a drop schedule. These documents explain the intended destination but are not executable evidence. To replace the deferral, implementation must perform the iterator conversion and structured loop/match elaboration, and annotated tests must directly inspect that completed shape, including conversion before iteration and matching that controls iteration termination. Pattern binding and loop-body checks alone would not satisfy those requirements.

All claim aspects remain explicitly deferred. No specification weakening or N/A exception is needed. Performed source inspection through review start/read only; no source edits or behavioral tests were performed, and centrally executed suites remain separate evidence. No requested edits: current TODO evidence honestly records the pending implementation and fixtures.
